name: Fibre
what_is: Fibre is carbohydrate that is not digested or absorbed in the small intestine. Different types of fibre behave differently in the digestive system.
why_botia: The fibre value on a nutrition label depends on how fibre is defined and declared in that market. BOTIA keeps the declared value separate from the regulatory definition and evidence used to interpret it.
can_1: Read the fibre value when it is declared on the nutrition label and preserve its unit and basis.
can_2: Keep fibre separate from carbohydrate when the applicable labelling system declares them separately.
can_3: Connect the declared value with the applicable regulatory information and documented evidence.
cannot_1: Determine the proportions of soluble and insoluble fibre unless the label declares them separately.
cannot_2: Assume fibre values from different markets are directly comparable without checking the applicable definition.
cannot_3: Determine an individual's fibre requirement from the nutrition label.
cannot_4: Treat an undeclared fibre value as zero.
